races.name: Ronan & Tom Gibbons Memorial Apprentice Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Femme Beauty
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 11f on Good ground for K J Condon with Max Popan (7lb claim) aboard; the lone front-runner here and likely to get a completely uncontested lead on Good To Yielding, which suits her proven stamina profile — her STYLE_FIT score reflects she races prominently rather than truly from the lead, but in this field that distinction barely matters.
runners_data.comment: Third at Limerick most recently, Femme Beauty is effective at today's trip on soft and good ground and looks well placed dropping in grade — first-time headgear adds interest. The concern is a run of form without a win, but the profile is solid enough to make her a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Rose Sienna
runners_data.note: Lightly raced filly (OR 120) returning after 247 days off for Sean Davis, with only one run on Good going and a tendency to fade in the finish — the long absence and stamina question over 1m1½f on yielding ground make her a significant unknown despite the high official rating.
runners_data.comment: A slow-away last-place debut at Leopardstown is the only form to go on, and now equipped with cheekpieces, Rose Sienna needs a very different showing to get involved here. Winless and with a speed rating well below the principals, she faces a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Delusional
runners_data.note: Placed third over 11f on Good ground 12 days ago for Daniel McLoughlin with Sam Coen's 2lb claim; a genuine hold-up type whose best form comes over middle distances, and the Good To Yielding surface should not inconvenience a horse with turf and easy-ground runs in the book.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with first-time blinkers and dropping back in trip from the 12f test that found him out at Limerick last time, Delusional showed better form prior and is effective at 8–11f on good and AW. Yet to score in recent starts, he is a danger if the headgear sharpens him on a more suitable distance.

runners_data.name: Zitkala Sa
runners_data.note: Has a placed effort at 10f on Good and ran in this sphere 21 days ago; a true closer in style, Paddy Harnett takes the ride and the horse is slotted into midfield on the map only because the field is overwhelmingly rear-loaded — the likely slow tempo is a real concern for delivering a winning finish.
runners_data.comment: Third on handicap debut at Gowran Park last time out, Zitkala Sa is effective at today's trip on yielding ground and wears a tongue-tie for the first time. Top-rated here and open to improvement from that encouraging debut run, the one reservation is that she remains without a win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Balance Of Trade
runners_data.note: Shows place form on Soft ground and has run over 8-10f on yielding-type surfaces; another genuine hold-up type pushed forward on the race map by weight of numbers at the rear — Rory Mulligan's 2lb claim adds appeal, but the absence of a strong gallop to chase down limits this horse's most dangerous scenario.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Gowran Park last time, finishing well late from off the pace, Balance Of Trade is proven at today's trip and acts on heavy and yielding ground. Inconsistency is the caveat — winless in recent starts — and a wide draw in first-time cheekpieces adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Cameclose
runners_data.note: Recorded a fourth-place effort over 10f on Standard ground and returned just 8 days ago for Jack Davison; flags a tendency to fade in the finish which is amplified on Good To Yielding, and while naturally a closer, the compressed race shape here means sitting closer than ideal without the tactical switch being a genuine positive.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up the field and well held in a Cork handicap last time, Cameclose has it all to prove on that evidence but tries first-time blinkers and stays this trip among others; the headgear would need to spark a much sharper, more prominent showing for him to enter calculations.

runners_data.name: Kart Of Gold
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness has a notably active 14-day strike rate (2/33) and Jack Kearney takes the ride; however, this horse's recent form string (70090) shows persistent near-last finishes, the fading-in-finish flag is concerning on a yielding surface, and the OR of 45 reflects a horse operating well below the field's average ability.
runners_data.comment: A modest showing at Gowran Park last time is difficult to ignore, and Kart Of Gold arrives in the bottom tier of the field on ratings with a low speed figure. First-time headgear is the hope, but difficult to make a case without more convincing form.

runners_data.name: Music And Song
runners_data.note: Thomas Dowling's runner carries bottom weight and has form over 10f on Good and Soft but a consistent pattern of finishing in double-figure positions — the fades-in-finish flag combined with a 21-day break and Jack Cleary's inexperienced claim makes this the most exposed and lowest-rated runner in the field.
runners_data.comment: Tried in blinkers and well beaten at Gowran Park last time, Music And Song has given no indication of the ability needed to figure at this level. Winless in recent starts and ranked lowest in the field, prospects look limited.

races.paceDynamic: Femme Beauty is the lone confirmed front-runner here and should face zero meaningful pressure for the lead on a track that will be riding Good To Yielding throughout the card, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop over 1m1½f. With the rest of the field dominated by hold-up types — Zitkala Sa, Cameclose, Balance Of Trade, Kart Of Gold, and Music And Song all natural closers — the pace is unlikely to be pressured or accelerated significantly from off the front, meaning Femme Beauty can dictate every yard at her own rhythm. The field holds far more hold-up horses than can realistically operate from their natural position; with only one confirmed pace-setter, horses like Cameclose and Balance Of Trade who might prefer to be nearer the pace may find themselves closer than usual simply through the absence of a competitive gallop to track. This race shape — a lone leader setting a measured tempo on soft-ish ground — classically benefits the prominent or tracking profile, rewarding the horse that can press or sit just behind the pace, rather than true hold-up types who need a stronger gallop to pick off tiring rivals.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Femme Beauty Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Femme Beauty is allowed to stride clear from the gates and dictate an uncontested, comfortable tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: If Femme Beauty is allowed to stride clear from the gates and dictate an uncontested, comfortable tempo throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Struggle Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and the hold-up brigade are denied the strong gallop they need to deliver a finishing burst.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely slow and the hold-up brigade are denied the strong gallop they need to deliver a finishing burst.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Picks Up Late Ground
scenarios.trigger: If the pace does quicken meaningfully in the straight and one of the hold-up types produces a strong sustained run on the Good To Yielding surface.
scenarios.body: If the pace does quicken meaningfully in the straight and one of the hold-up types produces a strong sustained run on the Good To Yielding surface.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stops, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves falsely slow and then a bold move mid-race causes Femme Beauty to collapse in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves falsely slow and then a bold move mid-race causes Femme Beauty to collapse in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Femme Beauty's early jumping and stride pattern is the key — if she breaks cleanly and immediately sets a controlled gallop with no challenger, the race may effectively be over inside the first quarter mile.

Monitor Zitkala Sa and Balance Of Trade's early positions: both true closers pushed into midfield on the map, and if they drift back to their natural rear positions the pace shape becomes even more one-dimensional in Femme Beauty's favour.

Rose Sienna's fitness after 247 days off is a live danger — if this filly has been freshened purposefully by Sean Davis and travels smoothly through the race, the high OR of 120 suggests residual class that could overhaul anything late.

Cameclose returned only 8 days ago and carries a fading-in-finish flag — watch whether Wesley Joyce attempts to get this horse closer to the pace earlier than usual, which would be a telling tactical signal that the stable expects a slow tempo to neutralise this runner's hold-up limitations.

Ground confirmation: the Going Report consistently reads Good To Yielding across all 1m1½f races on the card — no significant drying or softening trend is evident, so current going assessments for each runner can be taken at face value.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Median Auction Maiden (Median Auction Race)

runners_data.name: Sron Na Caise
runners_data.comment: Effective at 8–10f on soft and needing to bounce back from a below-par Dundalk effort, Sron Na Caise has the experience of today's distance and could improve dropping into this grade. The worry is that her most recent run was well off her best and a return to form is required.

runners_data.name: Wonderfulwonderful
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up and once third in her recent flat starts, Wonderfulwonderful is proven at 7–11f on a sound surface and is respected returning to the flat after hurdles. First-time cheekpieces are a variable, and the question is whether she can recapture that placed form after fading out late last time over hurdles.

runners_data.name: Camino Lad
runners_data.comment: Third on debut at Limerick, Camino Lad shaped with clear promise and looks open to significant improvement at his second start. Trainer in red-hot form at 45% over the past fortnight, he acts on good-to-yielding ground and steps up in trip today — a move that looks a plus. Yet to score but taken to go close.

runners_data.name: Nermal
runners_data.comment: Second at Down Royal last time, beaten just 1¼ lengths over 10f, Nermal is effective at 1m–10f and handles good and AW ground. Consistent at his best and open to further progress, the main caveat is a trainer out of form at 3% in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Swing Street
runners_data.comment: A Golden Horn gelding out of a dam very useful at 9f, Swing Street has some pedigree credentials, though his half-brother was only moderate at 11f. Unraced and meeting experienced rivals, this is a demanding ask on debut.

runners_data.name: The Monday Club
runners_data.comment: An Invincible Army gelding with no form to go on, The Monday Club faces a demanding task on debut unless market confidence suggests otherwise. One for the notebook at this stage.

runners_data.name: Time Whisperer
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on debut at Gowran Park over a mile but showing a degree of promise, Time Whisperer steps up in trip today — a move that looks a plus on breeding. Acts on today's going but needs a clear step forward to figure.

races.name: Lodge At Ashford Castle Maiden

runners_data.name: Believe Again
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a single run on record, finishing unplaced at 10f on Good; a natural hold-up horse whose connections will find it difficult to position this runner where it wants to be in a field this congested, and the sole form run gives little confidence at this level.
runners_data.comment: Down the field at Roscommon on debut, Believe Again has experience of today's distance and going but that performance left plenty to prove. Faces a stiff task here and must show considerably better.

runners_data.name: Big Dispute
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with five career runs, all in maiden company, and a placed record that includes a third on soft ground — the most experienced horse in the field and Kevin Coleman's light 14-day record is not a concern here; trips up to 20f on Good suggest stamina is not the issue, and patience from the rear is the likely approach.
runners_data.comment: Fourth on his last flat outing and only easing late back up in trip over hurdles at Listowel last time, Big Dispute is effective at 10f on good-to-yielding ground. A return to the flat looks the right direction and he holds a reasonable chance here — just needs to find a bit more.

runners_data.name: Coul Dreamer
runners_data.note: W McCreery's five-year-old showed a flash of form with a third at 8f on Good and has soft-ground experience, but the horse's instinct is to race from the back of the field and, with several others wanting the same territory, finding a clear run at Ballinrobe's tight home turn will be a test for W J Lee.
runners_data.comment: Third at Roscommon on her penultimate start and with form at 8–10f, Coul Dreamer is an interesting entrant stepping back into a maiden from a handicap. The difficulty is that her latest run at Leopardstown was well below form, and she may be vulnerable to fresher or more progressive rivals.

runners_data.name: If Not For Grace
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan takes the ride on this four-year-old who faded to fifteenth in a 10f Good ground maiden last time; the finishing-fade flag is a concern at this trip and there is nothing in the single run to suggest the horse handles being crowded in a bigger field.
runners_data.comment: Off the pace and well beaten on debut at Gowran Park, If Not For Grace remains all to prove on this evidence. Experience of today's distance is a mild positive but significant improvement is needed to feature.

runners_data.name: Mano Chicago
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's four-year-old is the race's sole pace-maker, with form showing four runs including two runner-up finishes at 10f on Good and Soft — the tongue-tie is in place, and while placed at a mile, stepping up to 1m1½f on yielding ground is an open question; the STYLE_FIT flag acknowledges the longer trip may stretch a horse that has shown speed rather than stayingpower.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Dundalk last time by just three-quarters of a length in first-time blinkers, Mano Chicago is consistent and effective at 10–11f on soft and good — with a trainer in form, he arrives as a genuine contender. That slight frustration in not converting when close is the only concern, and the headgear stays on here.

runners_data.name: Mischievous Fun
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides this lightly-raced four-year-old who has two runs on record, both at 17-18f on Good where she finished well beaten; the finishing-fade flag and the drop back from those marathon trips to this middle-distance is a notable angle to monitor, though the return from a 44-day absence adds an unknown.
runners_data.comment: Below form on bumper debut at Killarney, Mischievous Fun faces a tough enough task making her flat debut here. The limited evidence offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Take Me
runners_data.note: Colin Keane aboard this Noel Meade four-year-old who has the most versatile unknown style of the field — the tongue-tie is noted, and form of 554 at 9-10f on various surfaces including a fourth at Hea suggests a horse capable of running a solid race; Meade's 3/15 fourteen-day record gives trainer-form support and this could be the dark horse in a prominent-tracking scenario.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with more encouragement at Dundalk last time, beaten four lengths over 11f, Take Me is effective across a wide range of going and wears a tongue-tie for the first time. Proven at today's distance and with a genuine chance again, the main caveat is that she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Western Bandit
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners this Anthony Mullins four-year-old who has failed to place in four starts including a fifteenth on Soft, and while the tongue-tie is worn, the horse's running style means it needs everything to go right positionally in a field already crowded with hold-up types; style-fit concerns are real.
runners_data.comment: Seventh at Dundalk last time over a mile, beaten seven lengths, Western Bandit is effective up to 11f and acts on yielding ground — the step up in trip today looks the right direction. A fourth-place penultimate run offered more, but consistency has been elusive in first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Cuckaloo Hill
runners_data.note: Leigh Roche's mount for M Flannery, wearing a tongue-tie, has a form string of 8-0400 across 10-12f including a fourth at 10f on Good at Ballinrobe — that course form is the one positive, but the horse is a natural hold-up runner squeezed into a midfield slot and the finishing-fade flag compounds the challenge.
runners_data.comment: Proven at 10f on good ground and fitted with a tongue-tie for the first time, Cuckaloo Hill was below form at Fairyhouse most recently and requires a bounce-back. Has shown enough on better days to place, but the recent trend makes it hard to be confident.

runners_data.name: Drowsy Maggie
runners_data.note: Nathan Crosse rides this four-year-old for Gerard Kyne on a first career start — zero form to assess, going suitability unknown, and a single Kyne runner in the 14-day stats means there is genuine uncertainty here; lightly-raced debutantes on yielding Ballinrobe ground are a lottery and the unknown flag is appropriate.
runners_data.comment: A James Garfield filly out of a dam moderate at 6f, Drowsy Maggie is a half-sister to How Far who was useful over shorter. The breeding suggests she may want further in time, but with no form to assess, she is not one to favour on debut.

runners_data.name: Harana
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes partners D K Weld's four-year-old who is placed in three of three career starts including a second at 8f on Soft and a third at 12f on Good — the natural prominent style suits this race shape precisely, the step to 1m1½f on Good to Yielding looks tailor-made for a horse that has already shown it stays 12f, and the parachute headgear is already established.
runners_data.comment: Back in a maiden after a handicap experience that proved beyond her at Leopardstown last time, Harana has placed third at Roscommon earlier and is effective at 8–12f on soft and good. Wearing a hood for the first time, this drop back in class and possibly more settled conditions looks a better opportunity — she is respected on her earlier form.

races.paceDynamic: Mano Chicago is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner maiden over 1m1½f on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Ben Coen can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits without being harassed through the early stages. The pace is therefore likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than truly searching, meaning those tracking the leader in second and third will race in a sweet spot throughout. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can physically place at the rear — Believe Again, Western Bandit, Coul Dreamer, and Cuckaloo Hill are all natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, and several of them will struggle to find their preferred late-running positions in a race that simply won't have enough horses in front to race around. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a moderate, even tempo — overwhelmingly favours prominent-tracking types like Harana who can latch onto Mano Chicago's backside through the middle stages and have something left to quicken at the line; pure closers dependent on the pace collapsing face a structurally hostile scenario here.

scenarios.title: Mano Chicago Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Mano Chicago is allowed to stride to the front unchallenged and sets a measured, even gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: If Mano Chicago is allowed to stride to the front unchallenged and sets a measured, even gallop throughout.

scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Harana or another prominent-tracking type moves to press Mano Chicago from the half-mile marker, lifting the tempo into the straight.
scenarios.body: If Harana or another prominent-tracking type moves to press Mano Chicago from the half-mile marker, lifting the tempo into the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so moderate through the middle stages that the field bunches and hold-up horses with genuine finishing pace emerge late.
scenarios.body: If the tempo is so moderate through the middle stages that the field bunches and hold-up horses with genuine finishing pace emerge late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Sorts Field
scenarios.trigger: If the ground is riding more yielding than advertised and the pace proves testing enough to find out those without the necessary stamina for this 1m1½f trip.
scenarios.body: If the ground is riding more yielding than advertised and the pace proves testing enough to find out those without the necessary stamina for this 1m1½f trip.

watchPoints.text: Mano Chicago's ability to see out 1m1½f on Good to Yielding is unproven at this trip — if Ben Coen goes too fast too soon trying to exploit the lead, the front-runner could stop sharply inside the final two furlongs and scramble the entire race shape.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Believe Again, Western Bandit, Coul Dreamer, Cuckaloo Hill) all wanting the same ground at the rear could cause significant interference or traffic problems rounding Ballinrobe's tight home turn — watch for Shane Foley and W J Lee in particular being blocked.

Drowsy Maggie is a complete unknown on debut for Gerard Kyne — debutantes at Ballinrobe on yielding ground can occasionally bolt up at big prices if well-prepared, and the absence of any form data means this runner cannot be confidently placed in any scenario.

Take Me wore a tongue-tie and has form at Hea (Heaphy) suggesting ability on differing surfaces — Colin Keane is worth following through the race for how aggressively he positions this runner, as any move to track Mano Chicago prominently would signal confidence from a top jockey who rarely takes rides without a plan.

Big Dispute's seven-year-old profile and long 59-day absence (including a missed jockey note) is worth monitoring in the paddock — a horse this experienced returning fresh in maiden company at Ballinrobe either arrives cherry-ripe or is ring-rusty, and the paddock read will be informative before this race.

races.name: Michael Joyce Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Daler
runners_data.note: The confirmed front runner here; wins on soft going and has sim-going form, but his OR=82 style tag shows he is racing slightly out of true role as a prominent type forced to lead — Keane will ensure he travels kindly and if he does, this distance and ground suit.|
runners_data.comment: Landing a handicap at Leopardstown last time by 2¼ lengths in a new headgear combination, Daler showed he is capable in his best form and is effective at 7–9f on a variety of going. Now wearing a tongue-tie and hood combination again, the 7lb rise in the weights is the key test — proven course and distance ability makes him a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Grey Leader
runners_data.note: Recorded a win over 9f on Heavy and has placed on Good, so the Yielding surface is not a concern; 58 days off for R P Burns who fires 1/7 in the 14-day window suggests sharpness is there, though the hold-up style needs a genuine gallop to deliver.|
runners_data.comment: Three consecutive below-par runs make Grey Leader very hard to fancy here, despite a win in the book and an effective range of 7–10f on heavy and good. He returns off a short break still needing to find that earlier form — inconsistency is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Mocking
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides a horse that won over 10f on Soft and has a string of placed efforts over similar trips — the drop to 9.5f is worth monitoring, but the softening ground suits and J P Murtagh's 5/29 T14 strike rate suggests selective deployment.|
runners_data.comment: Sixth at Cork last time over 12f in solid-enough form, Mocking is effective at 10–12f on soft and good and is fitted with first-time cheekpieces after a 50-day break. The trainer is in decent form and there is a suggestion he is capable of a similar effort here — one to respect for place prospects at least.

runners_data.name: Dark Summit
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan takes the mount on a horse flagged for fading in the finish — a concern over this trip on Yielding ground; the form string of 7-8000 shows a horse that has struggled to reach the levels suggested by an OR of 77 in recent starts.|
runners_data.comment: Consistently below form on his Irish starts since moving from France, Dark Summit's best efforts have come at 8f on the softer side of good — this trip looks beyond his comfort zone. Hard to make a case without a more encouraging recent run.

runners_data.name: Dark Viper
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners a prominent racer with sim-going form of 13/15 and a win in the record; the distance (10f was tripped last time) may be on the short side here but a forward pitch suits the likely race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Leopardstown last time and in the midst of a poor run of form, Dark Viper is effective at 6–8f on heavy and good. The first-time hood is new and a bounce-back is needed — the trip here may be on the long side given his best form has come over shorter.

runners_data.name: Marmeladova
runners_data.note: K J Condon's runner has genuine winning form on Good ground and was second last time, but as a true hold-up type re-mapped to midfield, she will need to work harder to find cover than her natural style demands — that is a subtle cost in a race not run to suit closers.|
runners_data.comment: Winning her maiden here earlier in her career and effective at 7–10f on a sound surface, Marmeladova makes her handicap debut off a mark of 75 that looks fair. Fourth at Gowran Park last time in a good fillies and mares event, she looks open to further progress settling into handicap company and there could be more to come.

runners_data.name: Justenzia
runners_data.note: Two consecutive placed efforts over 10-13f suggest she stays well, but Ballinrobe's 9.5f trip on Yielding ground is slightly sharp for a horse whose recent finishes have come over longer; Denis Hogan saddles her 11 days after last run, fresh enough.|
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up earlier but well beaten in her last two starts at Leopardstown, Justenzia is effective at 8–12f and is at her best with cut in the ground. A bounce-back is needed and she remains winless in recent outings — the drop back to this level is the hope.

runners_data.name: Merlin The Wizard
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle, arguably the standout jockey booking in the race, rides a horse that won over 12f on Good last time — the natural closer's instincts are squeezed by a busy hold-up division, so the rider's ability to find a path late may matter more than the horse's own pace.|
runners_data.comment: Landing a claimer at Limerick last time by 1¼ lengths over 12f, Merlin The Wizard is versatile at 7–12f and acts on yielding and good ground — a top course jockey takes the ride. The step back into handicap company is a stiffer ask and more will be needed to win this type, but recent winning form is a positive.

runners_data.name: Storm Averted
runners_data.note: 244 days off is a significant flag; the tongue tie is retained and the trainer hits 1/3 in the 14-day window but this horse's hold-up profile, true form over shorter trips and the long layoff combine to make it a speculative runner at best in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth at The Curragh on his last run a long 244 days ago, Storm Averted is effective at 7–8f with some give and wears a tongue-tie for the first time. An erratic profile makes him hard to trust after a lengthy absence, though the headgear and drop in class could prompt a better showing.

runners_data.name: Flying Fortress
runners_data.note: Jack Kearney (3lb claim) rides for Gavin Cromwell; prominent style suits the likely race shape and the horse has winning form over 8f on Flat, though sim-going stats (13/15 without a win) suggest the Yielding surface may blunt the finishing effort.|
runners_data.comment: Effective at 8–10f with cut in the ground and fitted with first-time blinkers, Flying Fortress tried over a shorter trip at Gowran Park last time and beaten 4¼ lengths. Reverting to a more suitable distance today, with previous winning form at this type of trip, he is open to improvement and is a genuine danger if bouncing back.

runners_data.name: Lough Leane
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good and was placed at 8f on Heavy, so the ground and trip have some match — but as a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot by the overcrowded closer division, Leigh Roche will need to manufacture a run that the race shape may not naturally provide.|
runners_data.comment: Below form 15th at Leopardstown last time — beaten 52 lengths off the same mark — Lough Leane has a win on his penultimate start and is effective at 8–12f on heavy and good. A major bounce-back is required and first-time headgear is the hope, but the scale of that last run is very hard to overlook.

races.paceDynamic: Daler is the sole confirmed front runner in this 11-runner field and, with no genuine rival to pressure him from the off, Colin Keane can dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over the 1m1½f trip on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe. The prominent types Dark Viper, Justenzia and Flying Fortress will press forward behind him, giving the race a structured shape rather than a chaotic early scramble, but none are likely to force Daler off his rhythm. Several true hold-up horses — Marmeladova, Merlin The Wizard, Storm Averted and Lough Leane — are displaced to midfield on the pace map because the rear of the field is overcrowded with closers; those runners will not all find their natural pitch and some will inevitably race closer than ideal. A controlled, honest gallop on softening ground over this distance shapes this race as one where prominent racers travelling within themselves and kicking off the turn will be advantaged — pure closers relying on a strong pace to create daylight face a structural disadvantage given the lack of genuine pressure.

scenarios.title: Daler Dictates, Prominent Wins

scenarios.body: If Daler sets a measured pace unchallenged and the race is run at a steady-to-honest tempo that rewards horses travelling prominently.

scenarios.body: If the gallop is stronger than expected and the prominent types flatten out, giving the true hold-up horses a genuine pace to close into.

scenarios.body: If the race develops with a moderate pace that fragments the field, allowing a midfield tracker to make a sustained run from two furlongs out.

watchPoints.text: Merlin The Wizard's jockey booking is the most significant in the race — Dylan Browne McMonagle on a hold-up horse in a closed-up field means watch for a wide run or switch to challenge late; if a gap appears, this horse can travel.

Storm Averted returning from 244 days off in a handicap with a hold-up style and genuine pace concerns — monitor in-running for any sign the layoff has blunted its ability to quicken; it could be used as an early market mover.

Dark Summit is flagged for fading in the finish and carries that concern into a race where the ground is yielding and the trip is 9.5f — Seamie Heffernan needs to produce it earlier than recent runs suggest it is capable of sustaining.

With four or five genuine hold-up types forced into midfield by the race shape, watch the early stages for crowding and position battles between Marmeladova, Lough Leane, Storm Averted and Merlin The Wizard — any scrimmaging in the first two furlongs will compound the disadvantage for closers in this moderate-tempo contest.

Daler's early sectionals will set the entire race — if Keane allows a soft opening half-mile, the race shape strongly compresses in favour of prominent types and the hold-up runners will find the ground coming too quickly in the straight.

races.name: J.J. Burke Peugeot Handicap

runners_data.name: Sands Castle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Adrian Sexton and Shane Foley who has a worrying tendency to fade when asked for her effort in the closing stages; 17 days since last run and three finishes outside the top 10 in her last three suggest she needs everything to fall perfectly.|
runners_data.comment: Proven on today's going at 1m, Sands Castle was off the pace and well beaten at Fairyhouse last time and remains without a win in recent starts. Needs to take a step forward, and the step up in trip today is a question mark given her best form has been over the minimum.

runners_data.name: Onyeisi
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides for Karl Thornton and this one has shown consistency placing without winning — four places from 13 runs on similar ground — but the step back from 10-12f trips to 9.5f queries whether the stamina that has kept him competitive at longer trips translates here.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Fairyhouse last time on better ground after a switch to that surface, Onyeisi is proven at 10–12f on AW and good and holds a fair mark on his UK form. First-time blinkers are a new element — capable of building on that latest effort and a genuine danger here, though he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Flagstone Lady
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for M D O'Callaghan, who has been in good form at 2/15 over 14 days; limited form over only three runs and a habit of finishing weakly flags a question mark, though the top jockey booking is the headline angle.|
runners_data.comment: Held up off the pace at Gowran Park last time without ever landing a blow, Flagstone Lady usually races from off the pace — the step up in trip today may suit her hold-up style better. Winless in recent starts and below the leaders on ratings, she needs improvement to trouble them.

runners_data.name: A Pretty Penny
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan partnering for Deborah Cody is a notable booking, and a flat-out winner last time over 10f on good ground gives this one solid claims; four places from eight runs on similar surfaces add confidence, and she is the one with the most obvious form profile for this trip and these conditions.|
runners_data.comment: A winner at Ballinrobe on her penultimate outing and running close to her mark in fifth at Gowran Park last time, A Pretty Penny is effective at 8–10f on a sound surface and returns to familiar conditions. Proven over course and distance, this looks a prime opportunity for her to go close again.

runners_data.name: Tavarua
runners_data.note: Went in a visor last time for K J Condon and has finished outside the top six in all three career starts; a true hold-up horse whose natural position at the rear is compromised by the mapwide congestion, meaning W J Lee will need to improvise tactically — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 tempers expectations.|
runners_data.comment: Off the pace and beaten nine lengths at Down Royal last time, Tavarua wears a visor for the first time and is open to improvement now entering handicap company. Proven over today's distance and going, the new headgear could sharpen her — a danger if it has the desired effect.

runners_data.name: Brave Approach
runners_data.note: Jarlath Fahey's string has two winners from 10 runners in the last 14 days and Nathan Crosse gets the leg up on a horse returning after only 10 days; this one recorded a sole win over 8f on standard Dundalk and has finished outside the frame in six of seven turf starts, with the redistribution meaning it races outside its comfort zone at the rear.|
runners_data.comment: Below form at Fairyhouse last time and ranked among the outsiders on our figures, Brave Approach won over 8f and is effective on AW ground. Dropping in trip here is a plus, but a bounce-back is required to figure in this competitive field.

runners_data.name: Rodeo Blues
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the mount for Joseph O'Brien whose yard is in strong form at 10/68 over 14 days, giving this one the best trainer-jockey combination in the field; form on soft ground (6th at Leopardstown on soft) is the most relevant piece, though all five recent runs end without a win and the horse is asked to race forward of its natural berth.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten 4¼ lengths at Leopardstown last time, Rodeo Blues is effective at 9f on yielding and soft and carries the top jockey-trainer combination — a significant positive at Ballinrobe. There looks to be further improvement in her, and that booking makes her a notable danger, though she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Connova
runners_data.note: Ms Sheila Lavery's charge is partnered by Robbie Colgan and has dropped steadily in OR to 45; best effort was a fourth over 10f on good ground in only four career starts, and the horse's genuine hold-up inclination is pushed forward by the field dynamics — the style compromise at 0.90 reflects real positional risk.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Gowran Park last time, beaten eight lengths, Connova is effective at 6–9f and acts on today's going. The longer trip today is at the limit of her best form — she has placed before but needs more to trouble the leaders here.

runners_data.name: Cause I Like You
runners_data.note: Luke McAteer rides for Michael Mulvany, who has fired in two from 18 over the last fortnight; fitted with a tongue-strap for the first time and freshened after only 8 days, the horse's best recent effort was fourth over 8f at The Curragh but it races out of its natural hold-up role in this congested field.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten 9¼ lengths at Cork last time and clearly best at shorter trips, Cause I Like You faces a stiff stamina test over today's longer distance and was well off the pace on that occasion. First-time headgear is the one positive angle, but the trip and recent form make it hard to be enthusiastic.

runners_data.name: Perggosa
runners_data.note: Off the track for 72 days — the longest absence in the race — and Keith Henry Clarke has had minimal recent runners (0/1 in 14 days); form figures of 0-09 are unpromising and only one of three runs has come on comparable going, making this one of the harder runners to assess with confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Off for 72 days and well below form at Bellewstown on her last start, Perggosa faces a tough enough task here. The pedigree offers a combination of speed and stamina on either side, but the form gives little to build on — no obvious case to make.

runners_data.name: Canon Law
runners_data.note: Robyn Donaghue-Leahy takes a 7lb claim for Brendan Duke, who is winless over 14 days (0/5); the form string 0005-0 reads poorly, and although there is a rare fifth-place peak in the history, this horse has finished outside the money in four of five recent starts on good ground — the claim is the main tactical angle.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten and giving little late at Gowran Park last time over a longer trip, Canon Law is effective at 7f on heavy ground and needs a drop in distance to show her best. Today's trip looks on the long side — hard to recommend without conditions more in her favour.

runners_data.name: Sand Art
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes partners for Kevin Coleman (0/7 in 14 days) and the form figures of 90-877 represent consistency at modest handicap level without threatening the places; best efforts came over 7f on good ground and the slight drop in trip from recent starts could help if the sprint-finish scenario develops.|
runners_data.comment: Keen but running to form at Down Royal last time, beaten 6½ lengths, Sand Art is effective at 7f–1m and the step up in trip here may help if she settles better. Winless in recent starts and outside the leading ratings, she is an each-way outsider at best.

runners_data.name: Wedding Year
runners_data.note: Cillian Rowan takes a 10lb claim for Adrian McGuinness, who has been profitable at 2/33 over 14 days; fitted in a tongue-tie and showed placed form over 8f on standard ground, while his most competitive runs (3rd, 4th, 5th) have come on artificial surfaces — the natural hold-up style is a positional burden in this field.|
runners_data.comment: Off the pace and well beaten at Gowran Park last time, Wedding Year is effective at 7–8f and acts on AW — this trip and headgear for the first time are new angles. The mark looks fair if she can bounce back, but consistency has been absent in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Honey Dale
runners_data.note: Rory Mulligan claims 5lb for Paul Mulligan and the yard has had zero runners in the 14-day window; form of 7-9505 includes a fifth over 7f on soft which is the most relevant piece, and the horse has shown enough in similar-going conditions (4 from 8 in the places) to feature if the sprint-finish lottery breaks right.|
runners_data.comment: Fifth at Down Royal last time, beaten 5½ lengths, Honey Dale is at her best over 6–7f and the step up in trip today could suit if she relaxes. Winless in recent starts and rated below the leaders — the trip is the key hope.

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: No jockey listed in the data — a flag worth monitoring before betting; Michael Mulvany has two winners from 18 recently, and this horse's entire form profile is built on soft/yielding ground (8 runs, all on soft or yielding), making it the standout beneficiary if the going deteriorates further through the evening card at Ballinrobe.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Leopardstown last time off a 3lb higher mark, close to her best, Nephin Mountain is effective at 7–9f on soft and good. Racing again just four days later is the main concern — the form is there if the quick turnaround is not an issue.

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this 15-horse field rated as a hold-up or midfield type, there is no confirmed front-runner to set any meaningful early pace, and the race will almost certainly drift into a dawdle before erupting into a mass sprint finish from the home turn. The entire complexion of the race hinges on which jockey blinks first and commits to make the running — likely a reluctant leader dragged into it rather than a natural front-runner dictating. Good-to-yielding ground at Ballinrobe over 1m1½f will reward stamina and those who travel economically in the drift, but the sprint-finish nature of this shape means a horse with a sharp turn of foot in the closing stages holds a structural advantage over pure stayers. This field holds significantly more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Tavarua, Nephin Mountain, Rodeo Blues, Connova, Cause I Like You, Perggosa, Canon Law, Sand Art, Wedding Year, Brave Approach and Honey Dale are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, with none of the above likely to secure a truly restrained position when there is no natural leader ahead of them; the horses most likely to accidentally assume the front are whoever draws low and gets shuffled forward by the slow early fractions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls for the first half mile and the race degenerates into a furlong-and-a-half dash, favouring horses with the sharpest turn of foot regardless of OR.
scenarios.body: If the field crawls for the first half mile and the race degenerates into a furlong-and-a-half dash, favouring horses with the sharpest turn of foot regardless of OR.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Grinders
scenarios.trigger: If the going rides slower than official Good-to-Yielding and genuine stamina becomes the separator over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the going rides slower than official Good-to-Yielding and genuine stamina becomes the separator over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Brave Front-Runner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one jockey, facing a wall of hold-up types, elects to kick on from halfway and steal a decisive lead before the field wakes up.
scenarios.body: If one jockey, facing a wall of hold-up types, elects to kick on from halfway and steal a decisive lead before the field wakes up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a runner drawn high drifts into an uncontested position on the outside and benefits from a clean passage while the field bunches on the inside rail.
scenarios.body: If a runner drawn high drifts into an uncontested position on the outside and benefits from a clean passage while the field bunches on the inside rail.

watchPoints.text: Nephin Mountain has no jockey declared in the race data — confirm market move and booking before committing, as a last-minute top rider booking here would significantly upgrade its claims given the going profile.

A Pretty Penny holds the only recent win in the field (1st over 10f on good ground) and Seamie Heffernan's booking for Deborah Cody makes this the standout form horse — watch for significant market support that could compress her SP dramatically.

The going at Ballinrobe has been described as Good-to-Yielding for all seven races on the card — by the time this 7:27 race runs, the ground will have been raced on heavily all evening; monitor any late going update that shifts the official description, as it would materially benefit Nephin Mountain and Onyeisi.

With 15 hold-up horses and no natural front-runner, watch the first furlong for a chaotic bunching scenario — any horse drawn in stalls 1-4 risks being squeezed back even further than its natural position, while those drawn double-digit could accidentally inherit the lead.

Rodeo Blues holds the highest-profile trainer booking (Joseph O'Brien, 10/68 in 14 days) and Dylan Browne McMonagle is the most accomplished jockey in the field after Keane and Heffernan — watch the market for this one drifting or tightening as an indicator of yard confidence on the day.

races.name: GAIN The Advantage Series Handicap

runners_data.name: Dutch Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up galloper for Noel Meade carrying a blinkered headgear flag; best recent run was 9th over today's 14f trip on Good but has been finishing weakly of late, and the one-pace Ballinrobe straight with a controlled gallop does not set up a big finish from the back.
runners_data.comment: Regressive and well beaten at Fairyhouse most recently, Dutch Gold arrives without a win in recent starts despite being effective at 10–12f. First-time blinkers represent an attempt to spark improvement — the ability may still be there but the downward form trend is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Daboya
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner for R Donohoe; has won over 16f on Good and should cross unchallenged to the lead — STYLE_FIT flag notes a slight out-of-role concern at a higher-pressure pace, but in this race that pressure is minimal, making its prominent tag more a natural asset.
runners_data.comment: Consistent if unable to find the front, Daboya ran on strongly late at Gowran Park last time, beaten seven lengths. Effective at 8–12f on the flat and fitted with first-time blinkers, she has a reliable profile and could perform well again — just needs a bit more to land one.

runners_data.name: Metamorphic
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly trained by Mrs John Harrington; 187 days off the track is the headline concern here, and while Shane Foley is a significant jockey booking, the drop back from a long absence into a big-field handicap over 13f on Good to Yielding with no recent form to judge is a significant negative.
runners_data.comment: Slowly away and well beaten at Dundalk most recently after a lengthy break, Metamorphic is proven at 9–12f on good ground and was in sound form prior to that run. A tongue-tie for the first time and a seven-month absence are the key unknowns — capable of better if returning in good order.

runners_data.name: Barrogstown Girl
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a strong record over today's 16f trip — three wins from six on Good or similar — but not seen on a track for 244 days and losing claimer Nathan Crosse's 5lb claim offers limited compensation; fitness is the only question mark against a horse whose trip and going profile are ideal.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a maiden hurdle at Punchestown last time, Barrogstown Girl must prove herself back on the flat, where earlier form showed promise — including runner-up at best. All to prove on this return to the flat discipline.

runners_data.name: Guy's Girl
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for W McCreery; most recent form is over shorter distances (8-10f), and today's step up to 13f on Good to Yielding is an unknown quantity — W J Lee rides but this is a horse that needs pace to aim at, which may be in short supply.
runners_data.comment: Modest form beaten 9¼ lengths at Fairyhouse last time, Guy's Girl is effective at 8–12f on a sound surface. Consistent without threatening the winner — needs more to land a race at this level.

runners_data.name: Coulstys Way
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with encouraging placed form over 14f on Good; Jack Kearney's 3lb claim on board helps at the weights, and just 10 days since his last run suggests the stable is bullish — the trip suits and the style fits perfectly for this controlled-pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Off form on her return at Fairyhouse last time, Coulstys Way has twice placed second in recent starts and is effective up to 14f. A bounce-back is required but there is ability in the locker — one to watch if she can recapture that placed form.

runners_data.name: Lagoon Nebula
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Andrew Kinirons who has run over today's 16f trip before; Luke McAteer takes the ride and the horse has form on Soft, making the going no concern, though recent efforts have lacked a telling finish.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Listowel last time, beaten 5½ lengths, Lagoon Nebula is effective up to 2m and holds a solid chance here if building on that consistent recent form. Proven at today's trip and going, she rates a genuine danger — the main caveat is remaining winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Master Sydney
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Paul W Flynn with a decent strike rate over this distance range on Good; 33 days fresh and Robert Whearty retained, but has been disappointing in recent outings and the slow gallop means it needs something to go wrong up front to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Badly interfered with and well below form last time out, Master Sydney has a clear excuse for that run and is effective at 12–16f. Yet to score in recent starts, he needs a clear passage and improvement — but that incident gives some reason to forgive the latest effort.

runners_data.name: Wolf Prince
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up stayer — two wins over 16f including on Soft ground — who carries the baggage of being a 10-year-old, but Nicola Burns claims 5lb and the horse's stamina profile is legitimate; 58 days off adds a minor freshness question.
runners_data.comment: Slow to find stride on his return to the flat at Navan last time after a two-month break, Wolf Prince has shown better form prior — third on the penultimate outing — and the step back up in distance today is a plus. Hard to be confident, but earlier form suggests he is capable of better.

runners_data.name: Bruant
runners_data.note: A natural rear-of-field galloper for A J Martin who has won over 19f on Good, but the redistribution here reflects a crowded back-end — the STYLE_FIT tag and fade-in-finish warning compound the concern that Robbie Colgan may not get a clear passage from a compromised position.
runners_data.comment: Capable of better and effective at 10–13f, Bruant has been slipping down the flat handicap ladder to an attractive mark and now wears a hood for the first time. Landing a hurdle at Downpatrick last time, he arrives with a recent positive and improvement is expected if the hood helps him translate that ability on the flat.

runners_data.name: Eternal Echo
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for David O'Sullivan; the U (unseated) in recent form is a flag and the trainer has had no runners in the last 14 days, suggesting a yard out of form — Declan McDonogh's quality booking keeps it in the conversation, but form is erratic.
runners_data.comment: Came down at the start last time — an isolated incident rather than a true form line — Eternal Echo has shown genuine ability in a placing prior and is effective at 10f. Needs more to win but the excuse is credible.

runners_data.name: Miss Gitana
runners_data.note: Prominent-going filly with Dylan Browne McMonagle taking the ride — a major booking for OR 63 — but the fade-in-finish warning is persistent across her form string and all five recent runs have ended in mid-to-rear finishes over today's distances.
runners_data.comment: Beaten eight lengths at Listowel last time on a longer trip, Miss Gitana is effective up to 2m and a top course jockey takes over here. Won on her penultimate start and has the ability to go well — but ranked among the outsiders on figures, a return to that form is required.

runners_data.name: Sonic Invader
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's mount for Noel Meade has shown his best form at 14-16f on Good, but he is a natural hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield map position; the STYLE_FIT discount applies and the stable's recent 3/15 strike rate gives only modest confidence.
runners_data.comment: Third at Listowel last time and runner-up the time before, Sonic Invader has posted consistent placed efforts and is effective at 8–16f on soft and good. Proven at today's trip, he rates a genuine each-way chance — just needs to turn those consistent efforts into a win.

runners_data.name: Miss Australie
runners_data.note: A true closer — winner over 12f on Soft — whose redistribution into midfield reflects the overcrowded rear of this field; Paddy Harnett claims 5lb but the horse's last four runs have produced two 10ths and an 11th, with the sole win on a contrasting surface profile.
runners_data.comment: Tenth last time on a longer trip — falling short on stamina off the same mark — Miss Australie drops in distance today, a move that suits given she is effective at 10–12f on soft and good. Won on her penultimate outing and the shorter trip is a positive, though the yard has been out of form of late.

runners_data.name: Miss Crinshawn
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride for Peter Fahey, and the filly has placed twice recently at shorter trips on Heathrow/Flat, but she is a natural hold-up runner shown in midfield by necessity and the step up to 13f on Good to Yielding is further than she has proven effective.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a neck at Cork last time off a 4lb lower mark, Miss Crinshawn has returned to form of late and is effective at 8–12f with cut or on AW. The trainer's strong record in this race adds further appeal — winless in recent starts remains the caveat, but she has come close and rates a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Makaiah
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who ran second last time over 12f on Good — the most recent meaningful form figure in this field — and has placed six times from 13 runs; no jockey listed is a minor concern but the trip, going and style are aligned for this pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 2½ lengths at Roscommon last time in an encouraging effort, Makaiah is effective at 12–16f on soft and good and looks capable of building on that form today. The trip suits and she has a genuine chance if reproducing that level.

runners_data.name: Covert Legend
runners_data.note: A hold-up type for Maurice Ahern who is 235 days off the track and whose entire recent history is over 10-11f on Flat/Standard — today's 13f on Good to Yielding is a significant step into the unknown on both trip and going, and the redistribution only reinforces the structural disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Beaten two lengths at Southwell last time off a 1lb lower mark, Covert Legend is effective at 9–11f and usually races from behind. After a 235-day absence, the return to a longer trip on turf is an interesting angle — returns to her last winning mark, though all her best form has come on AW.

races.paceDynamic: Daboya is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, with no genuine rival looking to dispute the lead, should be able to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over 1m5f on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe. The prominent types behind — Coulstys Way, Lagoon Nebula, Barrogstown Girl, Eternal Echo, Miss Gitana and Makaiah — will queue up in the early stages, creating a compact mid-race procession rather than a searching test of stamina. The field holds more hold-up horses than the map can place at the rear — Sonic Invader, Bruant, Miss Crinshawn, Miss Australie and Covert Legend are all true closers who are unlikely to settle as far back as their natural style demands, meaning the genuine rear of the field will be thinly populated. An uncontested, honest gallop set by Daboya over this extended trip on soft-ish ground strongly favours resolute prominent racers who can track the tempo, travel smoothly, and sustain their effort — late closers have less ground to make up on paper but face the problem that the pace is not genuinely strong enough to set them alight from behind.

scenarios.title: Daboya Dictates, Prominents Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Daboya sets an uncontested honest pace and the prominent trackers race into winning positions turning for home.
scenarios.body: If Daboya sets an uncontested honest pace and the prominent trackers race into winning positions turning for home.

scenarios.title: Daboya Bowls Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Daboya's uncontested lead stretches into a winning margin and the chasing pack fails to reel it in on the run-in.
scenarios.body: If Daboya's uncontested lead stretches into a winning margin and the chasing pack fails to reel it in on the run-in.

scenarios.title: Closers Catch Them Napping
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves slower than expected and one of the hold-up horses — despite being crowded at the rear — manages to produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves slower than expected and one of the hold-up horses — despite being crowded at the rear — manages to produce a sustained late run.

scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group races too keenly tracking Daboya and ties up in the closing stages, throwing the race open to the reshuffled midfielders.
scenarios.body: If the prominent group races too keenly tracking Daboya and ties up in the closing stages, throwing the race open to the reshuffled midfielders.

watchPoints.text: Daboya has no rival for the lead — watch whether Sam Coen (5) bowls along at a truly soporific clip, because if the pace is exceptionally slow the prominent trackers may be wrong-footed when the gallop quickens late.
Barrogstown Girl is 244 days absent but has three wins over today's trip and going profile — if she returns fit, she is the single biggest threat to the controlled pace shape playing out as expected.

Colin Keane on Sonic Invader and Ben Coen on Miss Crinshawn — two high-profile jockeys on horses redistributed out of their natural positions — watch whether they push forward early against their horses' natural instincts, which could inject unwanted pressure into the early stages.

Wolf Prince at 10 years old with two wins over 16f on Yielding-type ground is worth tracking from the rear in the straight — if the race falls apart for the prominent group in the final furlong, the veteran's stamina could see him finish through beaten horses.

Makaiah's recent second over 12f on Good is the freshest placed form in the race — watch how far off the pace the jockey settles it, as a prominent hold on the inside rail could prove decisive in a race with a hollow rear group.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Deressa
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner, likely to control early fractions unchallenged from stall draw; P Twomey sends her 30 days fresh but current stable form is modest (1/18 in 14 days), and her form figures (6480-0) are worrying — style fit is solid but recent results are not.
runners_data.comment: Well below form at The Curragh last time despite experience at today's trip and going, Deressa steps back up in distance with a tongue-tie for the first time. Effective at 10–12f with cut, the new headgear is a positive but the recent record makes it hard to be optimistic.

runners_data.name: Royal Hollow
runners_data.note: Best record in this field at this trip and going (3W9P at sim-going, wins at 1m6f and 1m7f on soft); 284 days off is the major concern, but Andrew Slattery trains and rides the mare himself, suggesting confidence — strong matchup on paper if fitness is there.
runners_data.comment: A winner at this trip and proven over today's going, Royal Hollow won a flat race two starts back and has run well over hurdles since — runner-up at Listowel last time in a decent mares' event. The step back to flat racing looks right and she is entitled to respect here.

runners_data.name: Denim And Diamonds
runners_data.note: McMonagle is a high-class booking for a hold-up filly who has struggled with shorter trips and faster ground; 48 days off, headgear noted (t), and inconsistent recent form (080-78) keep expectations measured, but 1m5f on Good To Yielding could unlock a better performance.
runners_data.comment: Connected with the top course jockey-trainer combination who have a strong record in this race, Denim And Diamonds is effective at 12–14f on good ground. She performed at her recent level in a high-class conditions race last time and remains winless in recent starts — the mark may need to ease further, but the positive conditions angle keeps her in the mix.

runners_data.name: Stellar Quality
runners_data.note: Progressive filly, 21 days fresh after a win, and all four runs on similar going have produced placed or winning efforts (1W3P); she wants to race prominently and should be able to secure a close-tracking position behind Deressa from the outset — compact form profile with no obvious distance or going concerns.
runners_data.comment: Third at Gowran Park last time, staying on well from a shorter trip, Stellar Quality is proven at 12–14f on a sound surface and looks open to further improvement after just four starts. A winner earlier in her career and stepping up to today's longer distance — a clear positive — she is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Switch From Diesel
runners_data.note: Won her last two starts at 1m6f on Good ground and wants to race up with the pace, but with Deressa and Royal Hollow also wanting the early positions, Colin Keane may find her further back than ideal; her genuine frontrunning instinct is the key angle, even if the map cannot always place her there.
runners_data.comment: Landing a novice hurdle by 4¼ lengths at Punchestown last time, leaving her rivals trailing in her wake, Switch From Diesel is a classy dual-purpose performer effective at 12f on heavy and good-to-soft. The significant jockey booking adds further interest on her return to flat action — the unknown is whether hurdling form fully translates at this mark.

runners_data.name: Thatwilldoso
runners_data.note: Three placed efforts at 1m on Good ground but recent form includes a 9th and a 0 at shorter trips; trainer Coleman has 0/7 over the last 14 days and, while she is a natural prominent racer, she is likely to find herself operating in an unnatural midfield position in this particular race shape.
runners_data.comment: Progressive over 10–12f and suited by give, Thatwilldoso has been off 50 days and needs to bounce back from a poor run at Cork. Twice runner-up in earlier form and on an easing mark, there is ability here — but more is needed to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Earthsong
runners_data.note: Won over 1m6f on Good ground 33 days ago and handles this conditions profile well (7/8 at sim-going); a hold-up operator who needs the pace to be honest to pick up late — the most naturally suited to the expected race shape if Deressa keeps things controlled.
runners_data.comment: Landing a handicap at Gowran Park last time by two lengths off a lower mark, Earthsong is effective at 12–14f on heavy and good and looks open to building on that form. Now on a higher mark, the question is whether she can maintain that progress — but the form is solid and she rates a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: La Dame Blanche
runners_data.note: At seven years old and OR 69, she is the lowest-rated runner in the field; a genuine hold-up type whose natural position is at the rear, though the redistribution note reflects the unusually crowded midfield — trainer has only one runner in the past 14 days and no win, and her recent form (508-74) offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Roscommon last time, beaten 6¼ lengths, La Dame Blanche is effective at 12–13f and holds an outside chance here. Winless in recent starts and rated below the main principals, she needs a step forward to pose a real threat.

races.paceDynamic: Deressa is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 1m5f heat and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should be able to set a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good To Yielding ground without ever being pressured into over-extending herself. Royal Hollow, Stellar Quality and Switch From Diesel all want to race prominently, but the map cannot accommodate all of them — Switch From Diesel is the most likely of the trio to concede ground and settle for a tracking position behind Deressa and Royal Hollow, with Stellar Quality and the re-routed Colin Keane mount scrapping for the early berths. This field carries more genuine front-running and prominent intent than the race shape can naturally absorb; Deressa is best placed to dictate, Royal Hollow has the course and distance form at this trip to sit close without over-racing, and Stellar Quality has the freshness (21 days) to challenge early. The race shape strongly favours a hold-up horse who can travel comfortably through the steady fractions and produce a sustained late run — with Earthsong and Denim And Diamonds best profiled to exploit that scenario, provided the honest but unspectacular pace does not collapse into a sprint finish that rewards only those drawn into a close position throughout.

scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Deressa dictates a controlled, uncontested tempo that sets up a decisive late challenge from the hold-up horses.

scenarios.body: If Royal Hollow and Stellar Quality push up assertively to sit on Deressa's heels and the pace quickens mid-race, leaving hold-up horses with too much to do.

scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Deressa is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a truly modest tempo and converts her lead into a front-running success.

scenarios.title: Midfield Squeeze Out
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes messy in the early stages with prominent types jostling for position and the pace collapses, producing a muddling contest that no one covers cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Royal Hollow has a 284-day absence to overcome, but her sim-going record (15/15 attempts, 3W9P) at this trip is the strongest in the race — watch to see if she moves fluently in the preliminaries and runs on well from halfway as the acid test of her fitness.

Switch From Diesel is a natural front-runner who will be pushed away from her preferred position by the number of prominent types in this field — watch whether Colin Keane elects to go forward regardless and what effect that has on early fractions if he takes Deressa on.

Deressa has posted three consecutive defeats (0, 4, 8) and her most recent wins came over shorter trips on faster ground; if she sets a soft, uncompetitive tempo rather than a genuinely honest one, the race could turn into a sprint that nullifies the hold-up horses entirely.

Earthsong won over 1m6f just 33 days ago and Declan McDonogh takes the ride — watch the market moves for this filly given her form profile is the best match to the expected race shape, and note whether she travels smoothly through the Good To Yielding ground in the early stages.

Ballinrobe's 1m5f course has a long run-in that historically suits horses who travel well through the race rather than those who need a late sprint — any sign of slow early fractions compressing the finish into the last furlong would benefit Royal Hollow and Stellar Quality over the pure hold-up types.
